html:
Tonlé Sap is the great lake of Cambodia, which grows several times in size each rainy season as the Mekong floods and pushes water back up the Tonlé Sap River, reversing its flow.

The flood carries fish into the flooded forests to breed, making the lake one of the richest inland fisheries in the world. Fish and the fermented paste prahok, with rice, have been the core of Khmer diet since Angkor, which stood on its northern shore.

The river's turn back to the sea is marked each year by the Water Festival in Phnom Penh. Dams upstream in Laos and China and climate change now threaten the flood pulse. See dams in Laos.
sum: Tonlé Sap is the great lake of Cambodia, which grows several times in size each rainy season as the Mekong floods and pushes water back up the Tonlé Sap River, reversing its flow.
